company_name: East Buy Holding Limited (東方甄選控股有限公司)
overview: East Buy is a Beijing-based private-label products and livestreaming e-commerce platform, spun out of New Oriental Education's after-school tutoring crackdown in 2021-2022 and chaired by New Oriental founder Yu Minhong. The company sells self-developed private-label agricultural, food, and household products primarily through livestreaming on Douyin (China's TikTok), supplemented by its own APP, WeChat Mini Programs, Taobao, JD.com, Pinduoduo, REDnote, and a small but growing network of offline experience stores. Having divested its original Koolearn education business (now continuing only as 'Private Label Products and Livestreaming E-Commerce'), East Buy is now almost entirely a private-label FMCG brand built on top of a livestreaming distribution engine.

business_model.summary: East Buy earns revenue from direct sales of its own private-label products (fresh food, snacks, health/nutrition, personal care, household, apparel) and resale of third-party branded goods via livestreaming content, converting viewers into GMV on Douyin and other platforms. A paid membership program on its own APP (launched October 2023) adds a smaller recurring-revenue layer with subscription fees and member-exclusive pricing. The company is explicitly shifting its model from 'traffic-driven' (reliant on a single star livestreamer) to 'product-driven' (building a durable private-label SPU catalog), after the costly loss of its signature host in 2024.

revenue_streams.name: East Buy APP (owned channel, incl. membership)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market consumers in China, skewed toward price- and quality-conscious households; paid membership tier adds a loyalty/subscription layer
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China only (Beijing HQ, sourcing from ~28 provinces); listed in Hong Kong (HKEX 1797), no material international revenue yet though FY2027 plans reference 'overseas markets' exploration

main_competitors: Other livestreaming MCNs/influencer-led brands (e.g., Li Jiaqi/Austin Li's Meiyan group)
competitive_position.market_position: A mid-sized niche player in China's vast livestreaming e-commerce market; GMV of roughly RMB10.2bn in FY2026 is a small fraction of Douyin or Taobao Live's overall livestreaming GMV, but East Buy has built one of the more recognized standalone private-label-centric livestreaming brands outside the major platforms' in-house ecosystems

moat_factors.description: The 'East Buy' brand built around Yu Minhong's reputation, a 'Three Highs' (safety, quality, value) quality promise, and cultural/educational content differentiates it from pure discount sellers, but brand equity was damaged by the 2023-2024 scripting scandal and star-host exit

Full-chain traceability system (raw material to delivery), over 26,000 quality inspection reports, and direct deals with 100+ manufacturers create some switching/replication costs versus fly-by-night livestreaming sellers
APP membership (353,000 paid subscriptions as of FY2026) is small relative to major platforms but growing and creates modest recurring engagement and higher per-customer value
Net cash position (~RMB5.8bn total monetary capital, debt/equity near zero) funds continued investment in warehousing, private-label R&D, and offline expansion without needing external capital

weaknesses: Heavy dependence on a single external platform (Douyin) for the large majority of GMV and traffic, with limited success diversifying to owned channels

History of key-person/influencer risk: the business was built around and nearly derailed by the departure of its star livestreamer (Dong Yuhui) in 2024, and core leadership (former CEO Sun Dongxu) has also departed (Nov 2025)
Small scale relative to e-commerce giants — limited bargaining power with platforms and suppliers compared to Alibaba, Pinduoduo, or JD.com
Brand reputation sensitive to recurring public-opinion controversies (scripted content scandal, pricing complaints) in a fast-moving, sentiment-driven livestreaming market
Nascent, capital-intensive offline retail and instant-retail pivot (stores, vending machines, warehousing) is unproven at scale

growth_drivers: Continued shift of GMV mix toward higher-margin private-label products (52.6% of GMV in FY2026, up from 43.8% in FY2025), expanding gross margin
Rapid SPU expansion (1,009 private-label SPUs as of FY2026 vs. 732 a year earlier) across new categories: health/nutrition, seafood, maternity/baby, personal care
Multi-platform diversification beyond Douyin: Taobao, JD.com, Pinduoduo, REDnote, WeChat Mini Programs/Mini Shops, and the owned APP

Omni-channel expansion into offline: experience stores (Beijing, Xi'an, Zhengzhou), vending machines (100+ units across 26 cities) leveraging New Oriental's nationwide campus network, and on-demand/instant retail launches in Shanghai and Beijing
Membership program growth and monetization (353,300 paid APP subscriptions in FY2026, up 34% YoY) with unified cross-channel benefits
AI-enabled customer service and sales-conversion tools (shopping-guide agents, large-model-driven conversion) to improve efficiency and reduce headcount costs
Planned FY2027 move to a 'systematic, matrix-based' private-label product strategy with phased international/overseas expansion
Large net cash balance (~RMB5.8bn) available to fund M&A, supply-chain investment, or further buybacks

business.description: The large majority of GMV still flows through Douyin; any algorithm, fee, or policy change by ByteDance could materially impair traffic and sales

The 2024 loss of star host Dong Yuhui caused GMV to fall ~40% and tipped the company into a loss; the business remains associated with founder Yu Minhong personally hosting livestreams, a continuing single-point-of-failure risk
A scripted-content scandal in late 2023 triggered a consumer boycott and leadership shakeup; Chinese livestreaming audiences are highly sentiment-driven and prone to rapid backlash
Offline stores, vending machines, and instant retail are new, unproven, and relatively capital- and management-intensive initiatives for a company whose core competency has been content/livestreaming
Former CEO/co-founder Sun Dongxu was removed from the CEO role in Dec 2023 and fully departed in Nov 2025; several livestreamers have also exited in 2026

financial.description: Revenue fell ~33% in FY2025 following the Dong Yuhui exit before rebounding ~30% in FY2026; earnings have swung from large losses to large profits within a few years
RMB-denominated operations with a HK-listed holding company; FY2026 saw an RMB99.4m exchange loss versus an RMB18.6m gain in FY2025
Analysts (CMB International) flag margin pressure from livestreaming-matrix expansion, private-label investment, and new offline store openings

regulatory.description: Livestreaming commerce in China faces increasing scrutiny over advertising claims, consumer protection, and platform fee practices; food/agricultural product safety claims carry compliance risk given the company's 'Three Highs' quality marketing

Ongoing commercial ties to New Oriental (campus vending machines/stores, historical EDU framework agreement, shared chairman) require disclosure and governance scrutiny as a connected-party relationship

regulatory.risk: China ADR/HK-listing delisting and capital-markets access risk
regulatory.description: As a Cayman-incorporated, HK-listed company with mainland operations, it is subject to evolving cross-border data, foreign-investment, and overseas-listing rules applicable to China-based issuers

macro.description: East Buy's value-for-money positioning is partly resilient to, but also partly exposed to, a cautious Chinese consumer and property-driven wealth effect slowdown
China's e-commerce/livestreaming sector remains intensely price-competitive (Pinduoduo, Taobao, Kuaishou, JD.com), pressuring margins across the industry
As a seller of fresh and processed agricultural products, input costs (produce, packaging, logistics) are subject to weather and commodity swings

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's livestreaming e-commerce market continues to grow but is maturing and consolidating around a handful of dominant platforms (Douyin, Taobao Live, Kuaishou) and influencers; private-label/house-brand penetration in Chinese retail is a structural growth theme as consumers seek value amid slower income growth
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - consumer discretionary/value retail blended with staple food and household products provides some defensiveness, but GMV has proven highly sensitive to content/host-driven traffic swings
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given net cash balance sheet; indirect sensitivity via Chinese consumer confidence and discretionary spending
key_input_costs: Agricultural raw materials (fruit, grain, dairy, seafood)
Platform traffic/advertising costs on Douyin and other channels

recent_developments.event: Co-founder and former CEO Sun Dongxu formally resigned, citing personal reasons; Yu Minhong publicly confirmed the departure and later succeeded him as legal representative of the main operating entity
Livestreamers 'Mingming' and 'Tianquan' announced resignations, continuing a pattern of on-air talent turnover

First offline experience store opened in Beijing's Zhongguancun (~400 sqm), showcasing private-label products (>75% of assortment) with traceability displays and tasting stations; reported better-than-expected early traction
Opened additional 'cooperative operation' offline stores in Zhengzhou and Xi'an in partnership with New Oriental campuses, and launched on-demand/instant retail in Shanghai and Beijing

FY2026 (year ended 31 May 2026) results announced: revenue up 29.8% YoY to RMB5.7bn, operating profit swung to RMB663.4m from an RMB109.9m loss, net profit up to RMB543.9m from RMB6.2m, driven by private-label mix shift (52.6% of GMV) and H2 acceleration (H2 revenue +53.7% YoY)

CMB International upgraded the stock to 'Overweight' with a HK$27 target price following a positive FY2026 profit alert, citing the private-label-plus-multi-channel strategy, while flagging near-term margin pressure from livestreaming-matrix and store expansion
Share buyback program (up to RMB500m authorized in 2024 in the wake of the Dong Yuhui departure) continued, with RMB167.4m of share repurchases executed during FY2026

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results (released August 2026, year ended 31 May 2026)

items.target: Shift from sporadic new-product launches to a 'systematic, matrix-based and cyclical' long-term product operation model, with phased domestic and overseas expansion
items.notes: Qualitative strategic guidance rather than a quantitative target; management has not issued formal revenue/margin guidance ranges in the filings reviewed

items.target: Continue expanding offline experience stores and nationwide instant-retail front warehouses
items.notes: Builds on 3 stores opened in FY2026 (Beijing, Xi'an, Zhengzhou) and vending-machine rollout (100+ units, 26 cities)

items.notes: No explicit subscriber count target disclosed; emphasis on renewal rate and satisfaction over raw membership growth

guidance.management_commentary: Management (Chairman/CEO Yu Minhong and CFO Yin Qiang) emphasized that growth momentum 'picked up remarkably' in H2 FY2026, driven by private-label investment, livestreaming matrix expansion (11 new/upgraded Douyin vertical accounts, 18 channels total), and operational refinement. Management reiterated a 'customer-centric' and 'user trust as the foundation' philosophy, stated membership strategy will prioritize renewal rates and satisfaction over scale, and signaled FY2027 will see private-label development 'comprehensively upgraded' alongside continued AI investment in customer service and sales conversion.

bull_case: Sharp margin and earnings recovery post-Dong Yuhui departure shows the business can rebuild profitability on private-label economics rather than a single celebrity host, with FY2026 net profit up nearly 90x YoY and H2 momentum accelerating
Structural shift toward private-label (52.6% of GMV, 37%+ revenue growth) carries higher, more controllable gross margins (35.8% in FY2026, up from 32.0%) than third-party resale
Strong net-cash balance sheet (~RMB5.8bn total monetary capital, minimal debt) funds organic reinvestment, buybacks, and optionality for M&A without dilution or leverage risk

Omni-channel and membership diversification (APP, offline stores, vending machines via New Oriental's campus network, instant retail) reduces reliance on any single platform and builds recurring, higher-value customer relationships

Brand/quality positioning ('Three Highs' standards, full-chain traceability, 26,000+ inspection reports) differentiates East Buy from low-trust discount livestreaming sellers in a Chinese consumer market increasingly focused on value-for-money and food safety
bear_case: The business has already demonstrated extreme fragility to the loss of a single influencer (Dong Yuhui), and continued reliance on founder Yu Minhong personally livestreaming, plus ongoing livestreamer/executive turnover (Sun Dongxu, other hosts in 2026), signals unresolved key-person risk
Douyin remains the dominant sales channel with limited diversification success to date, leaving East Buy exposed to platform policy, algorithm, or fee changes it cannot control

China's livestreaming and e-commerce sector is intensely competitive and price-driven (Pinduoduo, Taobao Live, Kuaishou, JD.com), constraining long-term pricing power and margin durability for a company with a fraction of their scale

New offline retail and instant-retail initiatives are unproven, capital-intensive, and represent a significant strategic pivot away from the company's original livestreaming-content competency, raising execution risk

Brand reputation has already been damaged once by a scripted-content scandal and consumer boycott, and the sentiment-driven nature of Chinese livestreaming audiences means a similar controversy could recur and rapidly erode GMV again
